name: Smith Hall
use: Office of Undergraduate Admissions; SHARPP (third floor); formerly the first women's dormitory
architect: G. O. Totten; built by Lewis Killam
style: Tudor/Gothic-influenced brick with stepped gables (from photos)

renovations.what: Annex built by soldiers of the vocational training camp
Renovated with funds left over from building the Gables

facts.text: Opened in 1908 as the first women's dormitory, given by Edith Onderdonk in memory of her mother, Alice Hamilton Smith.
Has been a women's dorm, an international house, and an administrative building.
Admissions lists Smith Hall, 3 Garrison Avenue, as its office.
SHARPP (Sexual Harassment and Rape Prevention Program) has moved to the third floor of Smith Hall.

verdict: The 1908 first women's dormitory, all stepped gables and white porches, now Admissions' front door.
notes: A search snippet said Admissions lists the Elliott Alumni Center as a temporary in-person visit location, but the contact page as opened does not say so; unconfirmed. Clio implies Smith is still a dormitory; it is not. The 'Center for Academic Resources' tenant (old data, archives) was not confirmed as current. The admissions page gives both 3 and 5 Garrison Ave. The 2013 photos show a well-kept three-story gabled brick hall.
judgeNotes: Photos show one of the more characterful brick fronts on campus. Exterior up a point from the old run.
